course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

topic.title: Semi-log Plots
topic.summary: Semi-log plots with a logarithmically scaled y-axis, why exponential data appear linear on them, and the linear model log_n y = (log_n b)x + log_n a that comes from y = abˣ.

variants.stem: The table shows a data set. A semi-log plot of the data graphs log y against x, where log is the common logarithm.

parts.prompt: Find the change in log y from x = 0 to x = 1. Round your answer to two decimal places.
Find the change in log y from x = 3 to x = 4. Round your answer to two decimal places.
Is an exponential model appropriate for the data?

solution: The values of log y are 1.000, 1.176, 1.301, 1.398, 1.477 for x = 0 through 4. From x = 0 to x = 1, the change is 1.176 − 1.000 ≈ 0.18.
From x = 3 to x = 4, the change is 1.477 − 1.398 ≈ 0.08.
Log y does not change by a constant amount (0.18 compared with 0.08), so the points of the semi-log plot do not lie on a line. An exponential model is not appropriate.

variants.stem: An exponential function is given by y = 7(3)ˣ. A semi-log plot of the function graphs log y against x, and the points lie on a line.

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line. Round your answer to three decimal places.
Find the vertical intercept of the line. Round your answer to three decimal places.
Use the line to find log y when x = 3. Round your answer to two decimal places.

solution: Take log of both sides of y = 7(3)ˣ: log y = log 7 + x log 3. So log y = (log 3)x + log 7, and the slope is log 3 ≈ 0.477.
The vertical intercept is log 7 ≈ 0.845.

variants.stem: A semi-log plot of a data set that follows y = a(b)ˣ is a line with equation log y = 0.3x + 2, where log is the common logarithm.

parts.prompt: Find b. Round your answer to three decimal places.
Find a. Round your answer to three decimal places.
For what value of x is log y = 2.9?

solution: For y = a(b)ˣ, the semi-log line is log y = (log b)x + log a. So log b = 0.3 and b = 10 raised to the power 0.3 ≈ 1.995.
Also log a = 2, so a = 10 raised to the power 2 ≈ 100.000.

variants.stem: The graph shows a semi-log plot of a data set, with log y on the vertical axis and x on the horizontal axis. The data follow y = a(b)ˣ, and the marked points have integer coordinates.

stimulusBlocks.caption: Semi-log plot of a data set, log y against x

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line.
Find b. Round your answer to three decimal places.
Find a.

solution: The line passes through (0, 3) and (1, 4). The slope is the rise over the run: 1/1 = 1.
The slope of the semi-log line is log b, so log b = 1 and b = 10.
The vertical intercept is log a = 3, so a = 10 raised to the power 3 = 1,000.

variants.stem: The table shows data that follow an exponential model y = a(b)ˣ, where a and b are positive integers. A semi-log plot of the data graphs log y against x, where log is the common logarithm.

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line through the first and last points of the semi-log plot. Round your answer to three decimal places.
Find the vertical intercept of the line. Round your answer to two decimal places.
Write the exponential model, using integers for a and b.

solution: The points of the semi-log plot are (1, 1.398), (2, 2.097), (3, 2.796), (4, 3.495). The slope through the first and last points is (3.495 − 1.398)/3 ≈ 0.699.
The vertical intercept is log y at x = 0: 1.398 − 0.699(1) ≈ 0.70.
The slope is log b ≈ 0.699, so b = 10 raised to the power 0.699 ≈ 5. The intercept is log a ≈ 0.70, so a ≈ 5. The model is y = 5(5)ˣ.

solution: Taking logarithms gives log C = (log 0.8)t + log 80, so the slope is log 0.8 ≈ −0.097.
The vertical intercept is log 80 ≈ 1.903.
Set C = 8: log 8 = (log 0.8)t + log 80, so t = (log 8 − log 80)/log 0.8 ≈ 10.3 hours.
